pr.title: AMX attention: serve kv_mul 16 (Muse Glimmer) with a group_heads template parameter

5623855297.body:
The shape here is right: one predicate shared by the gate and the kernel signature, the 4-head object code unchanged, and the kernel-case skip now visible instead of a WARN that passed. What holds it up is that none of it runs in CI at this head: no PR lane sets `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH`, so both AMX binaries run as their stubs, the 16-head epilogue has no assertion on its softmax state, and the new transpose lanes have no host-testable path. Details inline.

Not verified: none.

Coverage gaps:
- **Real-AMX execution of `check_qk<16>` and `check_pv<16>` at `4c4b7b8864`.** No CI lane compiled the option on; every review host lacked AMX; the author's record is `round3.log` on delphi-3bda, outside the repository. The reported assertion counts (17,425 with AMX, 4,111 with the kill switch) reconcile exactly to every section running, which corroborates but does not replace in-repo evidence. Still needed: per-section Catch2 output from a Granite Rapids host at this head, or a CI run with the option on landing on a delphi runner. Hand derivations and AVX-512 probes by eleven reviewers cover the transposing store only.
- **AMX-on compile and link at this head.** No CI run; four reviewers' local syntax-only compiles of the kernel TU, both test TUs and `t_llama_unit.cpp` under `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH` pass. Still needed: one linked build of both binaries, for example a manual `cmake-single-platform.yml` dispatch at the head.
- **Closed: `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF` build at the head.** Build Tron job 117831672410 compiled both test TUs with the option off and Test host ran them. This closes the OFF-build gaps raised by sequence/security@fable, full/tests@fable, sequence/denotational@fable, sequence/doctrine@glm and units/correctness@fable.
- **Reports resting on a false CI premise.** full/denotational@glm, units/haskell@glm, units/ponytail@glm, units/security@glm, units/doctrine@glm, sequence/ponytail@glm and sequence/denotational@glm stated that CI built with the option on and that the 16-head sections executed. The build log contradicts this. Their execution-evidence claims count for nothing; their code reading and probes stand.
- **Granite Rapids timing for the 16-head pack and transpose.** Findings 5 and 13 were measured on Zen 4 and via instruction counts. The PR-level Glimmer A/B exists in the author's record only.

Purpose: Justified. Next decision: whether any served head-128 model with kv_mul 8 runs CPU attention in production (if so, add 8 here rather than in a follow-up), and whether to close the benchmark provenance gap with an object compare of the `<16>` instantiation between `5061623a34` and head or one Glimmer rerun.

## Architecture

Ideal.

Approach: the three AMX attention kernels become function templates on `group_heads`, constrained by one constexpr predicate `group_heads_ok` ({4, 16}) that `shape_ok` also uses for the dispatch gate; the bodies stay in the single `-mamx` TU, are explicitly instantiated for both sizes, and the call sites pass the constexpr `geometry.kv_mul()`, with head size honestly fixed at 128 since the tile math is 128-specific.

Ideal: this is the shape I would pick; the gate and the kernel signature share one predicate, so a `kv_mul` that passes `eligible` can only name an instantiable kernel, enforced by the compiler rather than a caller remembering, and a miss in the instantiation list fails loudly at link.

Gaps:
1. `follow-up`: the set {4, 16} is a decision without a written reason. The kernels as written serve any multiple of 4 up to 16 (`amx_attn.cpp:215-216`, `:245-253`; pack and PV are plain loop bounds), so refusing kv_mul 8 (`t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:117-120`, whose comment about "above 16" does not explain 8) is a choice -- unvalidated on hardware? Either instantiate 8 or write why not, in `group_heads_ok`. While there, the first `static_assert` at `amx_attn.cpp:213` is a third copy of the set; the real transpose constraint is `% 4 == 0 && <= 16`, which the second one half-states. Replace the copy with the constraint.
2. `follow-up`: `amx_attn_h128g4` and `_128x4` now lie about the shape they serve, and `amx_attn_iface.hpp:14-16` says "kept" without a why. Comments describe what is. Rename to `amx_attn_h128` / `_128` in a separate mechanical PR.
3. `accepted`: two homes for the group set (predicate plus instantiation list) is the floor for out-of-line template bodies in a single `-mamx` TU; a single-home spelling via an `index_sequence` and odr-use is reachable but buys little over a link error. Note `README.ci.md:586-587` still says "skip with a warning" after the CMake comment moved to "reported as skipped" -- same sentence, two homes, already drifted.

Event: REQUEST_CHANGES, at least one confirmed finding is blocker or major.

5997064669.body:
Thanks for the review. Agreed on the architecture reading, and on the CI premise: no pull-request lane sets `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` at this head, so the two AMX test binaries ran their placeholder cases in CI. Point by point:

- **CI lane.** The stale sentence in the CMake comment and in README.ci.md is fixed. The Nix flag stays out of this PR: it changes what the model tests of the required lane exercise on Intel runners. Evidence for this PR: option-ON test records from Granite Rapids hosts, a run of the legacy CMake workflow at the final head, and the transpose test in the required lane. (Inline threads at src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:216.)
- **16-head epilogue state.** Added, in every section of `exercise_page`. (t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:209.)
- **Transpose lanes.** `transpose_scores<group_heads>` is now in an AVX-512-only header, with an ungated 4/16-head case that also runs in the pull-request lane. (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:156.)
- **Real-AMX execution at head.** Run on a Granite Rapids host (delphi-3b35) at the final head ddf843ad97, one command per section. The QK sections pass 4,096 assertions each (4 and 16 heads). The PV sections pass 2,561 and 4,097. The transpose sections pass 1,280 each. The whole of `t_amx_numerics` passes 21,521 assertions in 5 test cases. Under the kill switch 3 cases pass and 2 skip. The totals are in the Verification section. The result record also holds a JUnit report with one entry per section.
- **Linked AMX-on build.** Manual `cmake-single-platform.yml` run at the final head. It builds and tests with the option ON. It is run [44777748892](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/actions/runs/44777748892), and its test-host job ran on delphi-3bd6-0, a Granite Rapids runner (attempt 2, after attempt 1 on the AMD runner andoria-ee10-0). The kernel cases execute only on a Granite Rapids runner. Both attempts pass all 106 host tests. The job log has one line per test executable, so it does not list single cases.
- **OFF build.** The Verification row now cites the default CI run at the final head, [44777709823](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/actions/runs/44777709823). The guard move is described on the inline thread at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:51.
- **Granite Rapids timing.** No per-kernel number exists. The A/B record files stay outside the repository. A per-kernel timing on Granite Rapids is the first item of the kernel-performance follow-up issue #5511 (vectorised pack, stage-3 hoist, lazy pack).
- **kv_mul 8.** Yes, the llama-70b family and qwen-3-32b run CPU attention at tron's defaults. I still keep 8 out of this PR: every group size has to pass the full system tests before it is enabled, and this PR is scoped to Muse Glimmer's kv_mul 16. The reason is in the `group_heads_ok` comment.
- **Benchmark provenance.** No rerun. The numbers were measured on delphi-3bda, the machine of the nightly systems test, at 5061623a34. This PR's changes since that commit carry a low risk for performance: the kernel file compiles to the same instructions (object compare in the Verification section), and the two epilogue edits you asked for remove work. The head also contains main up to 3bea58b788, which the nightly systems test measures. That test measures Muse Glimmer and llama-3.1-8b throughput after the merge.
- **Gaps 1-3.** The first `static_assert` is now the lane bound, the `group_heads_ok` comment carries the reason for {4, 16}, the header comment carries the reason for the kept names (rename in #5021, with your spelling), and README.ci.md matches the CMake comment.

Replies with the texts are on each inline thread.

4356061055.body:
The 16-head pack is a scalar triple loop, and at the `-O3` the build uses it compiles to 512 `vpextrw` stores. On a Zen 4 that's about 660 ns per call against 71 ns for the 4-head instantiation, and it runs once per token per KV head before the dense predicate.

Not a blocker for this PR, but a vectorised version looks like a contained follow-up: per 32-dim step, load 16 rows of 16 dwords (one head each), run the 4-stage unpack/shuffle dword transpose, store 16 panel rows, and mask the stores to 4 columns for the 4-head instantiation.

4645384790.body:
🔴 A broken AMX transpose or Q packer can now show up as "skipped" instead of "failed" on the Granite Rapids runner, the only host that runs these kernels. Catch2 v3.7.1 exits with the count of failed assertions, so exactly 4 failed REQUIREs gives exit 4. The new SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4 maps that to a skip. Fix: remove the skip mapping for t_amx_numerics: SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4, the skip_return_code_4 label and both "skip_return_codes":[4] entries in config/test-benchmarks.json (lines 151, 494). An unfiltered run never exits 4, because the transpose and packer cases always execute.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Catch2 is pinned to v3.7.1 (cmake/versions.cmake:26). It returns 4 only when every test case was skipped. Otherwise it returns min(255, failed assertions), so 4 failed assertions also exit with 4. At runtime t_amx_numerics has four two-section cases: transpose (t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:72), packer (:369), QK (:379) and PV (:391). Each section stops at its first failing REQUIRE. A regression in transpose_scores or store_transposed_rows (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_transpose.hpp) fails the 4-head and 16-head transpose sections and both QK sections on an AMX host: exactly 4 failures. A packer regression fails both packer sections and both QK sections: also 4. ctest (SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4 at t/CMakeLists.txt:624) and bin/slice status_for_returncode (bin/slice:1208, via skip_return_codes [4] at config/test-benchmarks.json:151 and :494) report both as skipped, and CI passes. On the base branch exit 4 was a failure. Nothing checks Catch2's output to tell a real skip from 4 failures. The cause is exactly what you describe. The QK and PV cases `SKIP` when AMX is absent [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:317-319, :330-332]. Catch2 3.7.1 returns 4 when every selected case was skipped and the process was not started with `--allow-running-no-tests` [catch_session.cpp:350-353]; our registered command never passes that flag. `add_catch_test` registers the whole binary with plain `add_test`, so Catch2's own `catch_discover_tests` default of `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4` never applies; only the PROPERTIES we pass do [t/CMakeLists.txt:212-219]. Slice reads the skip code from the `skip_return_code_N` label alone [bin/slice:1508-1510], so both halves are needed, as doc/slice.md:296-305 says.

The registration:

```
# The QK and PV cases SKIP without AMX; a run that selects only them exits
# Catch2's code 4. SKIP_RETURN_CODE + the skip_return_code_4 label report
# that as skipped (ctest and Slice) rather than failed.
add_catch_test(NAME t_amx_numerics LIBRARIES tron pos_fake
  PROPERTIES SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4 LABELS fake)
set_property(TEST t_amx_numerics APPEND PROPERTY LABELS skip_return_code_4)
```

The second label is appended with `set_property`, the way `t_mwaitx_cliff` appends its label. One call cannot carry both labels. `add_catch_test` forwards its arguments unquoted, so a list such as `"fake;skip_return_code_4"` splits into two items. `set_tests_properties` then gets an odd number of values and stops the configure.

Verification, measured on a Granite Rapids host. The kill switch stands in for a host without AMX. With it, `TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 gen/t_amx_numerics "[kv_data]"` exits 4: 2 cases, both skipped. `ctest --show-only=json-v1` lists `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4` and the label `skip_return_code_4`. The unfiltered kill-switch run exits 0, with 3 cases passed and 2 skipped. The unfiltered run with AMX exits 0.

4646192229.body:
The mapping stays. Catch2 v3.7.1 does not exit with the count of failed assertions.

v3.7.1 standardised the exit codes. A run with a failed assertion always exits with 42, and 4 means only that every selected case was skipped [catch_session.cpp:37, :39, :350-356 of the pinned source]. Its release notes for 3.7.1 say "Assertion failures are now always 42". Both builds fetch that archive by hash [cmake/versions.cmake:26-27; t/CMakeLists.txt:5-6; flake.nix:1056-1058]. The exit code that counts failed assertions is the behaviour up to v3.7.0.

I ran your trigger at this head on a Granite Rapids host (delphi-3b35). The break: stage 1 of the transpose reads `_mm512_unpackhi_ps(r0, r1)` where it must read `_mm512_unpacklo_ps(r0, r1)`.

- `gen/t_amx_numerics` with AMX: the transpose and QK cases fail, with exactly 4 failed assertions. The exit code is 42.
- The same under `TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1`: 2 failed assertions, 2 cases skipped, exit code 42.
- `ctest -R '^t_amx_numerics$'`, which applies `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4`: `***Failed`, and ctest exits with 8.

Slice reports every exit code other than 0 and the listed skip codes as failed [bin/slice:1208-1213]. So ctest and Slice both report four failed assertions as a failure.

4646192533.body:
The facts are right: no workflow that a pull request triggers builds with `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH`. The thread at src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:216 has the same point, and my reason for keeping the flag out of this PR. With it ON, every eligible model test of the required lane would run the AMX kernels on an Intel runner and the AVX path on an AMD runner. That changes CI for every pull request.

The test file was behind the guard before this PR. The new sections are the ones the review asked for (threads at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:143, :209 and :305). They run in the CMake workflow (`cmake-single-platform.yml`), which builds with the option ON. README.ci.md describes its manual run on the final commit of a PR.

What ran at this head:

- That workflow: run [44777748892](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/actions/runs/44777748892). Its test-host job passes all 106 host tests on an AMD runner (attempt 1) and on a Granite Rapids runner (attempt 2). `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` is one of them.
- The new transpose case sits outside the guard, so the required lane runs it.

6257190288.body:
## PR Summary

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
**Medium Risk**
Changes core attention numerics and dispatch for new GQA group sizes; mitigated by expanded fake-kernel, transpose, and hardware numerics tests, but production token identity can differ when AMX is enabled versus the prior AVX path.

**Overview**
**Extends Intel AMX dense attention** from GQA **kv_mul 4** only to **kv_mul 4 and 16** (128-dim heads, bf16 Q), so models like **Muse Glimmer 30B** (32 query heads / 2 KV heads) can use the AMX path on eligible full pages instead of the AVX dotter.

Kernel APIs (`pack_q_group_128x4`, `qk_rowmajor_128x4`, `weights_times_v_128x4`) are **templated on `group_heads`**, with explicit **4- and 16-head instantiations** in `amx_attn.cpp`. QK score transpose moves to **`amx_attn_transpose.hpp`** (AVX-512 only) and is covered by new **non-AMX** tests. **`self_attention.hpp`** passes the model’s `kv_mul` into pack/QK/PV and streamlines PV output handling.

**Tests and CI:** `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` always compiles dispatch with **`TRON_AMX_DISPATCH`** and fake kernels (including 16-head and 32/2 KV-head cases); `t_amx_numerics` treats missing AMX as **Catch2 SKIP** (exit 4) with **`skip_return_codes`** in benchmarks config. **README.ci.md** documents which workflows enable AMX. Changelog notes faster Glimmer attention on Intel AMX hosts.

<sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 90a9110be5d2c6552267322c472902984dca8e0f. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

Thanks for the careful work on this, and for the detailed replies. Almost everything from our review is done, and we checked it ourselves: the kernels compile to the same instructions as before, and when we broke the new code in 14 different ways, your tests caught every one.

One thing keeps this at changes requested.

**The dispatch test does not run in the required CI lane.** With `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` off, `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` compiles to its placeholder case. So the new 16-head checks only run when someone starts the legacy workflow by hand.

Your reason for keeping the option out of the Nix build makes sense: it would change what the model tests exercise for every pull request. There is a smaller way that avoids that. The test can pass the define itself, the way `t_page_share_counters` does, so only this one binary sees it.

To save you the work, we made that change in #5606, on top of your head. With the option off the test then runs all 30,747 assertions, and it fails when we break the dispatch code. That is the only thing we are still waiting on.

Two smaller notes:

- The registration line we suggested for `t_amx_numerics` was wrong: it does not configure. What you did instead is right. Sorry for that.
- Everything else is fine with us, including the three items you moved to #5511 and leaving kv_mul 8 out.
